title: Fail-closed pre-push review with a round budget
summary: The pre-push review stops being advisory. `--warn-only` is removed, so `osf review run` now exits non-zero on a kept must-fix or should-fix finding and on a review that could not run; a new round budget in the journal state lets a push through after a configured number of failed rounds, while a could-not-run streak ends blocked with a message. A credential preflight decides a reviewer with no key and no login file before any worker starts, osf's own `.osf/` output is filtered out of the changed-file set so a review round cannot change the next round's lens selection, and the opencode reviewer moves from `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to its own `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (CI secret `OSF_REVIEW_OPENCODE_API_KEY`).

nodes.label: moon `review` task
nodes.subtitle: osf review run --if-enabled --work-item …
nodes.summary: The pre-push task drops `--warn-only` and passes the work item file. Its comment now says a kept finding or a could-not-run review fails the push, and that it gates the push, not the merge.

nodes.label: Builder agent
nodes.subtitle: develop run in its own workspace
nodes.summary: The agent that pushes. It can change its own workspace, which is why the pre-push result gates the push but never the merge.

nodes.label: `osf review run`
nodes.subtitle: review_run_cmd / review_run_exit_code
nodes.summary: `--warn-only` is gone from both run and reduce. The command now returns the exit code straight from `review_run_exit_code`, which counts rounds.

nodes.label: finish_review
nodes.subtitle: verdict + kept findings → exit code
nodes.summary: Prints the lines, writes SARIF, posts, then computes the code. A kept must-fix or should-fix finding forces 1 regardless of verdict; when `count_rounds` is set it consults the round budget and may return 0.

nodes.label: `osf review reduce`
nodes.subtitle: review_reduce_exit_code
nodes.summary: Same fail-closed rule as run, but passes `count_rounds = false`: the pull-request reduce step never spends the pre-push budget.

nodes.label: ReviewConfig
nodes.subtitle: in_sandbox_rounds, could_not_run_rounds
nodes.summary: Two new fields with defaults of 3 each, validated to be greater than zero. The whole-run default timeout drops from 2700s to 1800s.

nodes.label: setup
nodes.subtitle: changed files → lens selection
nodes.summary: Filters `.osf` paths out of the changed-file set before lens selection, so a review round's own counter or SARIF write cannot change which lenses the next round picks.

nodes.label: changeset_risk::changed_files
nodes.subtitle: untracked files minus .osf/
nodes.summary: Drops untracked paths under `.osf/` from the risk assessment, for the same reason: osf's own output is not part of the change a person made.

nodes.label: preflight_and_not_run
nodes.subtitle: credential check before any worker
nodes.summary: Decides whether a reviewer has no way to sign in. A reviewer already skipped for a more specific reason, or with no read-only mode, is not judged again. A preflight failure records every lens as could-not-run and starts no worker.

nodes.label: Reviewer::missing_credentials
nodes.subtitle: credential_env / login_paths
nodes.summary: Returns a reason when every credential variable is empty and every login path is absent under the real home. A templated reviewer is exempt, since a template may carry its own auth.

nodes.label: round_allows_push
nodes.subtitle: RoundCounts, RoundKind
nodes.summary: A pass clears the counts. A findings round increments and allows the push once past the limit. A could-not-run round increments and, past its own limit, returns an error naming the block instead of letting the push through.

nodes.label: review-rounds/<hash>.json
nodes.subtitle: journal state dir
nodes.summary: The counter file, named by a hash of the canonical worktree path so each develop run has its own count. It lives in the journal state directory, outside the worktree the builder can edit.

nodes.label: secret_values::held
nodes.subtitle: env vars + login-file leaves
nodes.summary: Now also collects every string leaf of each agent's JSON login file, so a provider key kept in opencode's auth.json is scrubbed from reviewer output like an env var.

nodes.label: AGENTS roster
nodes.subtitle: opencode credential_env
nodes.summary: opencode's credential variable changes from `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, matching its own provider key rather than the OpenRouter one.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: opencode job secret
nodes.summary: The reusable workflow's opencode secret is renamed to `OSF_REVIEW_OPENCODE_API_KEY` and passed into the container as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.

nodes.label: review_run integration tests
nodes.subtitle: budget, preflight, should-fix
nodes.summary: Replaces the warn-only tests with fail-closed ones: a blocker and a should-fix both fail, the budget lets the fourth round through, a could-not-run streak ends blocked, and a missing credential stops the run before any process.

edges.label: --work-item, no --warn-only
edges.summary: The pre-push task now invokes the fail-closed command; its exit code is what stops the push.
The builder's own shell runs the pre-push checkpoint, which is why the result is trusted for the push only.
Run passes `count_rounds = true`; reduce passes false.
The reduce step shares the kept-finding rule but never spends the pre-push budget.

edges.label: round limits
edges.summary: Reads `in_sandbox_rounds` and `could_not_run_rounds` from the trusted config root before consulting the budget.
Only when counting rounds; the returned bool decides between 0 and the base code.

edges.label: load / save / clear
edges.summary: The budget loads, increments and saves the per-worktree counter, and clears it on a pass.
Setup now filters `.osf` paths before selecting lenses.
Risk assessment no longer counts untracked `.osf/` output as part of the change.
Each reviewer is preflighted before a worker starts.
The preflight asks the reviewer whether it has any way to sign in.

edges.label: credential_env
edges.summary: The credential variable names it checks come from the roster, which now names `OPENCODE_API_KEY` for opencode.

edges.label: login_paths
edges.summary: The scrubber walks each agent's login paths to collect JSON string leaves as secrets.

edges.label: OPENCODE_API_KEY
edges.summary: The opencode job passes the renamed secret into the container and runs `osf review run --reviewer opencode`.
Integration tests drive four rounds to assert the budget's exit-code sequence.
A fake run with no credentials asserts exit 2 and a journal naming the missing key or login path.
